others.name: Frazier Life Sciences Public Fund, L.P.

lockup.summary: The company, its directors and officers, and holders of nearly all its stock agree not to sell for at least 180 days after the prospectus date without the lead underwriters' written consent. Some exceptions apply.

what: A drug company that is developing an oral medicine for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a heart muscle disease, and other serious heart conditions.
risks: The company is young, has lost money every year since it began, expects more losses, and may never make a profit.
Even after this offering it will need a lot more money, and may not be able to raise it on good terms.
Raising more money could reduce existing owners' shares, limit how the company operates, or force it to give up rights to its drug.
Regulators like the FDA take a long time and are unpredictable, and the company's business would suffer badly if it cannot get approval.
risks_note: The first 4 risk factors, summarised by AI.
